questions.explanation: Software project planning begins once the SRS is baseline-approved; the primary estimation objectives are software size, project cost/effort, development schedule/time, and required staffing. These estimates are related: size is an input to effort models, and effort and schedule estimates contribute to project planning and cost.

questions.question: Which one is not a size measure for software

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.2; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: Lines of Code (LOC), Function Count / Function-Point measures, and Halstead's Program Length ($N = N_1 + N_2$) are software-size measures. Function Count and the resulting Function Points are related steps, not interchangeable labels. Cyclomatic Complexity ($V(G) = e - n + 2P$), introduced by Thomas McCabe, is a structural complexity metric measuring the number of linearly independent paths through the control flow graph, not software size.
questions.question_ar: أي مما يلي ليس مقياس حجم للبرمجيات؟
questions.explanation_ar: cyclomatic complexity مقياس تعقيد بنيوي وليس مقياس حجم.

questions.explanation: The Function Count / Function Point Analysis (FPA) method was originally developed by Allan J. Albrecht at IBM in 1979 to measure the functional size of software from the user's perspective, independent of programming language or implementation technology.
questions.explanation_ar: Alan Albrecht هو من طور طريقة Function Count.

questions.explanation: Function Point Analysis decomposes a software system into five distinct functional information domain characteristics: External Inputs (EI), External Outputs (EO), External Inquiries (EQ), Internal Logical Files (ILF), and External Interface Files (EIF).

questions.explanation: Final adjusted Function Points (FP) are calculated by multiplying Unadjusted Function Points (UFP) by the Complexity Adjustment Factor (CAF): $\text{FP} = \text{UFP} \times \text{CAF}$.
questions.explanation_ar: القيمة تحسب بضرب UFP في معامل التعديل CAF.

questions.explanation: The Putnam Resource Allocation Model is founded directly upon Peter Norden's empirical observations at IBM, which established that manpower utilization throughout research and development projects follows a Rayleigh distribution curve over time.

questions.explanation: COCOMO is an acronym for COnstructive COst MOdel, an algorithmic cost estimation model that estimates software effort, schedule, and team size based on project size (KLOC) and cost drivers.

questions.question: Estimation of size for a project is dependent on

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.12; publisher key p. 498

questions.explanation: Software size is an intrinsic attribute of the system's requirements and functionality; it is independent of cost, schedule, or calendar time. In fact, cost and schedule are dependent variables estimated *from* the estimated size, not the other way around.
questions.explanation_ar: الحجم يقدّر من خصائص المشروع لا من التكلفة أو الجدول مباشرة.
